subject: Picking how to normalize coverage; and dealing with outliers

messages.author: 93445ad41a8474ff
messages.subject: Picking how to normalize coverage; and dealing with outliers
parts:
How do we decide whether to normalize coverage by the median or mean? 

An example of the coverage plots for our samples are here: https://www.dropbox.com/s/unvg1pkm51od913/G_d0.A_d0.coveragePlots.pdf?dl=0

They are in the following order for each of 10 samples:
1 - methylation stats
2 - raw coverage
3 - filtered coverage (removing sites with less than 10 reads, higher than 99.9%ile coverage)
4 - median-normalized filtered coverage
5 - mean-normalized filtered coverage

I get different results depending on the normalization mode chosen so would like some guidance on selecting the most appropriate method. 

We also have a couple of outliers for each set of comparisons - see a PCA plot here: https://www.dropbox.com/s/idx3zsh1n8eq2p2/PCA.png?dl=0 
Do you recommend that we just discard them? Is there some stricter way to determine when we should be discarding outliers? 

Thanks for any help!

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: Picking how to normalize coverage; and dealing with outliers
parts:
most people would filter by coverage without normalizing. the distributions looks similar if you look beyond 10X coverage and would remove stuff beyond 1000X.

For the outliers, I would also look at the clustering, and if they cluster with the other samples, I would look at batch effects, are they processed and/or sequenced different dates ? if so, removing them is one option, other option is to try to include batch effects as covariates in the model, we have code in the development branch for that but it is not something I would advertise for people to use yet.

Best,
Altuna
